Both are lysosomal storage diseases in the MONDO disease ontology, but no specific shared process was found. Treat this as a lead to check, not a match. Shared distinctive signs: mental deterioration, splenomegaly and dysphagia. Different gene (NPC1, not GLB1), so a treatment for one does not automatically work for the other.

Q01.answer:
The closest communities RarePath found, strongest first:

RarePath rates the link between mucopolysaccharidosis type 4B and GM1 gangliosidosis as "same gene". Caused by changes in the same gene, GLB1. Shared distinctive signs: abnormal iliac wing morphology, opacification of the corneal stroma and platyspondyly. The disease itself looks different: one gene can lead to different conditions. [F5]

RarePath rates the link between GM2 gangliosidosis (Sandhoff disease, Tay-Sachs disease) and GM1 gangliosidosis as "strong link". Their genes act in the same biological processes: CS/DS degradation and Keratan sulfate degradation. Shared distinctive signs: cherry red spot of the macula, coarse facial features and splenomegaly. Already studied together in 4 studies, including PRONTO (NCT05109793). Different gene (GM2A, HEXA and HEXB, not GLB1), so a treatment for one does not automatically work for the other. [F6]

RarePath rates the link between sialidosis type 2 and GM1 gangliosidosis as "strong link". Their genes act in the same biological processes: Sialic acid metabolism. Shared distinctive signs: cherry red spot of the macula, slurred speech and coarse facial features. Different gene (NEU1, not GLB1), so a treatment for one does not automatically work for the other. [F7]
